scope: Private managed recursive runtime backing; no recursive source admission or generated constructor bridge yet

implementation.publication: Copy immutable payload and retain existing backing dependencies before attaching invocation owner
implementation.projection: Retained leases validate stable type token, payload size and alignment, and independently retain indexed dependencies
implementation.cleanup: Intrusive allocation-free iterative final-reference release with atomic shared and duplicate edge retirement
implementation.failure: Temporary lease rolls back unpublished nodes and retained dependencies; cancellation and existing expected/unexpected errors preserved
implementation.allocation_model: Extends existing Backing/Invocation/AllocationLease; published nodes keep invocation ownership until ordinary cleanup

coverage: Immutable payload copies and checked type/size/alignment projection
Independent child lifetime after parent/invocation release
Duplicate edges and shared diamond tails with reference-count balance
Invalid constructor/dependency requests and bounded dependency count
Injected allocation failure and pre-existing error channels
Cancellation before construction and during publication race; no partial node or retained edge escapes
100000-link chain cleanup on a 256 KiB pthread stack with terminal-reference balance
Concurrent final release of independently retained roots sharing a tail
Existing allocation leases and invocation accounting
Existing compiled enums, managed payloads and local workers
qualification.format: New test passes clang-format --dry-run --Werror; git diff --check passes

limitations: Compiler must enumerate every owned field; arbitrary payload bytes are not a self-describing ownership schema
No compiler-emitted runtime bridge, constructor/projection/match/update integration yet
No recursive worker packet transport or language-level source admission
Reference-count inspection is a private diagnostic snapshot, not a uniqueness predicate
